fields.description: Njiwa sends WhatsApp messages for this site, through the account settled here. The events on the next tab are ready-made moments to send on, and every one of them is off until you turn it on. Your own code can still send whatever it likes by calling njiwa_frappe.api.send.

Untick to stop this site sending anything at all; your key and settings are kept. While it is off, an attempt to send fails with a message saying so rather than quietly doing nothing, so you find out from the error log instead of from a customer.
fields.label: Send messages through Njiwa

fields.description: One key is the whole connection. Paste it, save, then press Test connection: Njiwa answers with the numbers this account really has, so you find out here rather than at the moment a customer should have been messaged.
fields.label: Connection

fields.description: Create a key at console.upeo.ai under API keys, then paste it here. A key starting sk_live_ sends real WhatsApp messages. A key starting sk_test_ checks every request and stores every message but delivers nothing, which is what you want until you are sure. Njiwa shows a key once and stores only its fingerprint, so a lost key is replaced rather than recovered. Here it is stored encrypted and is not shown again after you save.
fields.label: API key

fields.description: Both of these are defaults, and nothing more. A call to njiwa_frappe.api.send that names its own sending number, or passes wait, ignores what is set here and decides for itself.
fields.label: Sending

fields.description: Which of your linked WhatsApp numbers sends, when the code asking for a message does not name one. Write it in full international form, digits only, like 254712345678. Leave it empty to use the number marked default in the Njiwa console, which is the right answer if the account has one number. Test connection lists the numbers this account actually has.
fields.label: Send from

fields.description: Leave this off. Njiwa answers the moment it has stored the message, then delivers it, retries a failure five times and reports the outcome, all without holding your site up. Turn it on only in a script you are watching, where you want the real result on screen: it waits up to 15 seconds for the message to be sent or fail. Turned on for a form save, it makes a person wait 15 seconds for something Njiwa was going to do anyway.
fields.label: Wait for the result

fields.description: Nothing in here needs changing to send a message. It is open for the few sites that were given a Njiwa address of their own.
fields.label: Advanced

fields.description: Where Njiwa lives. Leave this exactly as it is. It exists for sites that have been given their own Njiwa address, and changing it otherwise stops messages going anywhere.
fields.label: Njiwa address

fields.description:
Every message is plain text. Anything in braces is filled in from the document:
{first_name} — The first word of the customer's name, or 'there' if there is none.
{last_name} — The rest of the customer's name.
{customer_name} — The customer's name as ERPNext holds it.
{order_number} — The name of the document that caused the message, such as SINV-00042.
{order_total} — The document total, with your currency symbol.
{order_date} — The posting date, or the order date on a Sales Order.
{order_status} — The document's ERPNext status, such as 'To Deliver and Bill'.
{payment_method} — The mode of payment, where the document has one.
{items} — One line per row, as '2 x Blue shirt'.
{item_count} — How many items in total.
{shop_name} — The company on the document.
{order_url} — A link to the document on your website. It only opens for a customer who has a portal login, so leave it out unless yours do.
{admin_url} — A link that opens the document in your desk. Only put this in the message to yourself: a customer cannot open it.

A placeholder that does not exist, {order_no} say, is removed before sending rather than posted to a customer.

Cancelling cascades. Cancelling a Sales Invoice in ERPNext usually means cancelling its Delivery Note and its Payment Entry first, so a customer will hear about one cancellation once for every cancel event you have switched on. Pick the one document your customers actually know about.
fields.label: How the wording works

fields.description: Sent when a Sales Order is submitted or cancelled. Shops that quote and confirm before invoicing work from these; shops that sell over a counter never make one.
fields.label: Sales Order

fields.description: For shops that confirm an order before it is invoiced. It tells the customer you have the order and what it comes to.
fields.label: Order confirmed

fields.description: The message sent when an order is confirmed. Leave it empty and nothing is sent, whatever the tick box says.
fields.label: Order confirmed

fields.description: Worth sending. A cancellation nobody explained is what turns into a phone call.
fields.label: Order cancelled

fields.description: The message sent when an order is cancelled. Leave it empty and nothing is sent, whatever the tick box says.
fields.label: Order cancelled

fields.description: Sent when a Sales Invoice is submitted or cancelled. A credit note is a Sales Invoice with Is Return ticked, and it has an event of its own below rather than being sent as an invoice.
fields.label: Sales Invoice

fields.description: The one most shops want. The customer gets the invoice number and the amount where they will actually read it.
fields.label: Invoice issued

fields.description: The message sent when an invoice is issued. Leave it empty and nothing is sent, whatever the tick box says.
fields.label: Invoice issued

fields.description: Tells the customer they do not owe it after all. Read the note about cancelling cascading before you switch this on.
fields.label: Invoice cancelled

fields.description: The message sent when an invoice is cancelled. Leave it empty and nothing is sent, whatever the tick box says.
fields.label: Invoice cancelled

fields.description: Money going back. Saying so stops the 'where is my refund' message before it is sent.
fields.label: Credit note issued

fields.description: The message sent when a credit note is issued. Leave it empty and nothing is sent, whatever the tick box says.
fields.label: Credit note issued

fields.description: Only money coming in from a customer. A supplier payment and an internal transfer are Payment Entries too, and this never touches either of them.
fields.label: Payment Entry

fields.description: A receipt, sent the moment you post the payment. It is the message customers ask for most and the one that stops them ringing to check.
fields.label: Payment received

fields.description: The message sent when a payment is received. Leave it empty and nothing is sent, whatever the tick box says.
fields.label: Payment received

fields.description: A receipt taken back, which usually means a cheque bounced or the money was posted against the wrong customer. Leave it off unless you want customers told about your corrections.
fields.label: Payment cancelled

fields.description: The message sent when a payment is cancelled. Leave it empty and nothing is sent, whatever the tick box says.
fields.label: Payment cancelled

fields.description: Sent when a Delivery Note is submitted or cancelled. A sales return is a Delivery Note with Is Return ticked, and neither event fires for one.
fields.label: Delivery Note

fields.description: The 'it has left us' message. ERPNext will not tell the customer anything at this moment; this arrives where people actually look.
fields.label: Goods on their way

fields.description: The message sent when goods are sent out. Leave it empty and nothing is sent, whatever the tick box says.
fields.label: Goods on their way

fields.description: Tells a customer expecting a delivery today that it is not coming.
fields.label: Delivery cancelled

fields.description: The message sent when a delivery is cancelled. Leave it empty and nothing is sent, whatever the tick box says.
fields.label: Delivery cancelled

fields.description: One message when an order becomes real, to your own number rather than to a customer's. It is sent once per document, and never for a return.
fields.label: New orders

fields.description: Send me a WhatsApp message when an order comes in.
fields.label: Tell me about new orders

fields.description: Which document means an order is real in your shop. A shop that quotes and confirms should leave this on Sales Order. A shop that sells over a counter never makes one and should set it to Sales Invoice. Only the one you pick alerts you, so an order that becomes both tells you once.
fields.label: Count an order as real when I submit a

fields.description: Where that message goes. Digits only, separated by commas if there are several, and everybody listed gets their own copy. A leading zero is fine here: a recipient is read against your own sending number's country.
fields.label: Your WhatsApp numbers

fields.description: What that message says. {admin_url} is worth having here: it opens the document straight from your phone. Leave the box empty and nothing is sent, whatever the tick box says.
fields.label: Tell me about new orders
